invariant: A return whose resolved sender and receiver are the same participant is a dotted self-message, inheriting the activating arrow configuration and deactivating only when it owns an activation stack entry. Its horizontal constraint is against the adjacent participant or border, never against the same participant. Its vertical loop, live-segment width, group extent and paint use the self-message model.
causal_divergence: Java CommandReturn constructs an ordinary Message with reversed participants and a dotted inherited ArrowConfiguration, then attaches deactivation if there was an activating message. Step1Message selects its self path by participant identity and reserves getConstraintAfter/Before with the self arrow width plus live-segment thickness. Rust retains a Return event, resolves its owners, but routes equal indices through the nonadjacent multi-span branch. At participant zero, right-1 underflows; elsewhere the width is incorrectly assigned to a preceding pair. Even avoiding that index would leave Return's straight-arrow paint and no-loop vertical advance wrong.
planned_change: Retain the complete owning arrow configuration and whether a return owns deactivation in the resolved lifecycle context. Lower resolved self-return events to ordinary dotted self-message events in a render-local cloned model, then recompute geometry/lifelines through the existing self-message path. Preserve input source identity and event indices, never modify caller data or clamp/skip constraints. The lowering strictly reduces unresolved Return events, so any layout restart terminates. Add semantic equivalence tests for explicit dotted self-deactivation versus return syntax and fresh Java cases varying order, recursion depth, long labels and return ownership.
